Rachel Dolezal draws ire of transracial adoptees

I never would have thought how this story affects transracial adoptees. My SO has a similarly difficult situation--he was raised by a Mexican stepfather his entire life and considers him to be his dad. He has two younger siblings that are half-Mexican American. He grew up eating Mexican food, speaking Spanish, and going to Catholic School/church that was 99% Hispanic. His abuelita tells him he is Mexican because he is family and he's treated like all of her other grandchildren. Although he might identify with that culture, he'll always be a tall goofy white guy, and he'll always be perceived as such by everyone he meets.
While I have no respect for Dolezal, her situation has raised interesting questions about race, culture and where lines get drawn.

What is the most intelligent species of fish?

I don't know about most intelligent of all fish, but the most intelligent commercially-available fish you can keep is an Oscar. They're basically aquatic puppies.

They are capable of distinguishing between different humans, and will sometimes get so used to one human that they may refuse to eat if someone new feeds them. Very few fish can do that. They are also one of the very few fish you can keep than can be trained, just like a puppy.
